atoms.b: The ancient Greeks told many traditional stories, called myths, to explain the world around them. These stories featured gods, ((++heroes robots)) and mythical creatures. They often taught ((++moral maths)) lessons.

atoms.text: Heracles was the son of Zeus and a human woman. He is a hero of many Greek myths and is famous for his incredible strength and bravery.

atoms.text: As punishment for a crime, Heracles was given twelve nearly impossible challenges to complete. atoms.text: Another famous myth tells the story of Icarus. He was the son of a skilled craftsman, called Daedalus, and they were imprisoned together on the island of Crete by King Midas.

To escape, Daedalus created wings from feathers and wax. He warned Icarus not to fly too high or too low. Overcome by excitement, Icarus ignored his father’s warning and flew too close to the sun. The heat melted the wax in his wings, causing him to fall into the sea and drown.

The story is a warning against arrogance, recklessness and overestimating your abilities. The phrase “flying too close to the sun” originates from this myth and is used to describe someone who takes too many risks or becomes too proud, leading to their downfall.
